key_insight: Transporting a log-concave source to heavy-tailed or well-separated multimodal targets intrinsically requires large gradients, regardless of the generative model architecture.
engineering_relevance: These gradient barriers expose an expressivity–numerical stability trade-off when designing pushforward deep generative models.
method: Derive quantitative gradient and Jacobian lower bounds for heavy-tailed and multimodal targets.
Establish results under weaker regularity assumptions and target perturbations.
Propose bijective reparametrizations to reduce gradient burdens in density approximation.
evidence_signal: Numerical experiments support the theoretical analysis, but the abstract provides no datasets, benchmarks, or quantitative results.
watch_item: The reparametrization mitigation applies to density approximation and should not be assumed to remove barriers in generative sampling.
paper_title: Intrinsic Gradient Barriers in Pushforward Deep Generative Models
